title: Pharmacy Inventory Coordinator
location: McDonald Wright, Los Angeles, CA, US
description:
Program: Pharmacy

Department: Health Services

Reports to: Associate Director of Pharmacy Operations

Schedule: Monday-Friday 7:30 AM to 4:30 PM

Status: Non-exempt


CENTER’S MISSION: Building a world where LGBT people thrive as healthy, equal, and complete members of society.

DEPARTMENT SUMMARY: The Los Angeles LGBT Center’s Department of Health Services is one of the nation’s largest and most experienced providers of LGBTQ-specialized primary care and related services, Our mission to help LGBTQ people lead healthier, happier lives is supported by our comprehensive array of client-centered services including primary care, mental health, psychiatry, sexual health, pharmacy, case management, nutrition, clinical research, housing services and a food pantry. The Center is one of a handful of Federally Qualified Health Centers in the nation specializing in serving LGBTQ people.

JOB SUMMARY: The Pharmacy Inventory Coordinator performs all aspects of inventory management including drug ordering, creating/maintaining drug profiles in Pioneer Rx, price updates, perpetual and quarterly inventories, oversees inventory/maintenance of the automated filling equipment, and drug returns through the reverse distributor for all pharmacy, dispensary and clinic medication rooms at various locations. The Pharmacy Inventory Coordinator is also a member of the 340B compliance team.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Inventory Management

• Order, receive, and store all medications and supplies, including AM/PM orders and ScriptPro Robot items

• Monitor and maintain appropriate inventory levels, accounting for back-ordered items

• Perform monthly inventory counts and weekly perpetual inventory checks, including controlled substances and top 10 antiretrovirals (ARVs)

• Conduct random stock verifications and adjust quantities in PioneerRx as needed

• Remove and store expired medications separately; coordinate regularly with reverse distributor

• Review drug usage and PAR levels to proactively identify and resolve inventory issues

• Perform weekly drug backorder reviews and ensure proper documentation and communication


Data & Systems Management

• Accurately enter and update medication data in PioneerRx in accordance with Center procedures

• Maintain current system queues (e.g., ready for pick-up, ready for fill, return to stock)

• Complete and reconcile inventory-related invoices

• Maintain paperwork and filing systems in compliance with pharmacy laws


Medication Preparation & Dispensing

• Prepare and fill automated dispensing equipment daily, including loading vials, labels, and related supplies

• Complete floor orders, including purchasing and preparing items for pickup

• Order and follow up on FOA (fill-on-arrival) items and communicate with clients as needed

• Perform LAI (long-acting injectable) stock checks to ensure appointment readiness


Compliance & Quality Control

• Ensure proper storage of all medications, including refrigerator and freezer items

• Log and monitor refrigerator/freezer temperatures; respond to excursions and quarantine items as needed

• Collaborate with clinic staff to ensure compliance with the 340B program

• Participate in the 340B compliance team and support ongoing program requirements


Communication & Coordination

• Communicate with vendors regarding damaged items and ensure timely resolution

• Send weekly notifications to providers and staff about medication stock issues, especially for hormone therapies

• Monitor and respond to all inventory-related chats and emails in a timely manner

• Interact with patients, providers, staff, and external pharmacies in a professional and courteous manner

• Assist Financial Coordinators with tasks as needed

• Participate in meetings and collaborative discussions


General Support

• Help maintain a clean, organized, and safe pharmacy environment

• Perform other duties as assigned


QUALIFICATIONS

• Knowledge of or experience working with the LGBTQ community and familiarity with issues of particular relevance to LGBTQ people

• A passion for the Center’s work and its mission to make the world a better place for LGBTQ people

• Current California Pharmacy Technician License; National Pharmacy Technician Certification preferred

• Minimum 2 years of experience in a high-pressure professional medical environment and ability to work some evenings and weekends

• Strong inventory / 340b purchasing knowledge

• Strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills with a high level of attention to detail

• Ability to work with pharmacy applications and other software systems

• Working knowledge of Pioneer Rx preferred

• Bilingual skills a plus (English/Spanish fluency preferred)

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively with people of diverse races, ethnicities, nationalities, sexual orientations, gender identities, gender expression, socio-economic backgrounds, religions, ages, English-speaking abilities, immigration status, and physical abilities in a multicultural environment.


The Los Angeles LGBT Center is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to fostering diversity within its staff. Applications are encouraged from all persons regardless of their race, color, ancestry, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, sex, pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions, religion, disability, age, military or veteran status, including status as a victim of domestic violence, assault or stalking, genetic information (including family medical history), political affiliation or activities, medical or health conditions, and marital status.

The Center requires that all staff working in Health Services clinical site locations receive the most up-to-date Influenza vaccinations and strongly recommends that staff also receive the latest COVID-19 vaccine. Staff not working at any of the Center’s clinical sites are encouraged to receive the latest COVID-19 and Influenza vaccines but are not required to do so. For more information, please contact jobs@lalgbtcenter.org.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Platform
description:
About the Company:

We're not here to run campaigns. We're here to help businesses build legacies.

OOm is one of Singapore's leading performance digital marketing agencies, and we've been growing businesses since 2006. Across SEO, SEM, social, content, and web, we work as true partners to our clients. We are obsessed with their success, honest about what works, and relentless in our pursuit of results that last well beyond one quarter.

Over 8,000 clients. 30+ industry awards. A Premier Google Partner. A Meta Business Partner.

But more than the accolades, what defines us is how we work and who we work with.

We believe in winning together. That means we back great teams over individual stars, make bold calls over safe ones, and build for tomorrow even when today's demands are loudest. We move with conviction, we show up with grit and resilience, and we never stop growing because that's exactly what we ask of the businesses we serve.

The Opportunity

About Us

At our company, we're building a suite of modern business applications that help organisations work smarter through automation, intelligent workflows and AI-powered experiences. While AI is a key part of our products, great software is built on strong engineering foundations.

This role is suited for an engineer who enjoys solving complex system and data problems, not just building application features. We are looking for someone who can combine strong hands‑on engineering ability with architectural thinking. Someone who can build the foundations today while ensuring they do not become the constraints of tomorrow.

What You'll Do

This is a hands‑on engineering role at the intersection of backend engineering, data systems, and platform architecture. You will work on technically complex problems involving data integration, data modelling, distributed processing, and reliable backend services.

You will play a key role in shaping how data is collected, structured, connected, and made available across our products, while helping establish engineering patterns that can scale as the platform evolves.

You'll:

  • Design and build scalable backend services and data platform capabilities
  • Build systems that ingest, process, and integrate data from multiple internal and external sources
  • Design robust data models for complex and interconnected datasets
  • Develop mechanisms for linking, resolving, deduplicating, and reconciling records across systems
  • Build reliable APIs, integrations, and data processing workflows using synchronous and asynchronous patterns
  • Design for data integrity, traceability, performance, reliability, and scalability
  • Handle real‑world integration challenges including retries, duplicate data, partial failures, and recovery
  • Contribute to the architecture of multi‑tenant, data‑intensive SaaS systems
  • Own technical solutions from system design through production, identifying architectural risks and trade‑offs
  • Collaborate with Product and Engineering to translate business requirements into pragmatic, scalable technical solutions

The Talent

  • Minimum 5 years of professional software engineering experience, with strong backend engineering fundamentals
  • Strong proficiency in at least one backend programming language such as Python, TypeScript, Java, or Go
  • Strong SQL and relational database knowledge
  • Experience designing backend services and APIs
  • Experience designing complex data models
  • Experience building data-intensive applications or platforms
  • Experience integrating with third‑party systems and APIs
  • Experience designing reliable systems that handle failures and inconsistent data
  • Experience working with cloud infrastructure
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity, evaluating trade‑offs, and designing pragmatic solutions rather than over‑engineering for hypothetical scale.

title: MiCHEP Director of Strategic Initiatives & Operations
description:
Director of Strategic Initiatives and Operations

Michigan Consortium for Higher Education in Prison (MiCHEP)
Full-time | Primarily remote within Michigan | $80,000–$105,000 plus benefits

About MiCHEP

The Michigan Consortium for Higher Education in Prison works with colleges, universities, the Michigan Department of Corrections, and other partners to expand access to high-quality postsecondary education for incarcerated students. MiCHEP’s member institutions operate degree programs across Michigan correctional facilities and share a commitment to educational excellence, human dignity, successful transition and reentry, and meaningful economic opportunity.

MiCHEP has received a four-year, $2.66 million grant from Ascendium Education Group to lead a statewide systems-change initiative, Aligning Programs and Services for Justice-Impacted Students Across Michigan. The initiative will bring together higher education, corrections, workforce, reentry, government, and student partners to improve education, transition, reentry, and economic opportunity for incarcerated and formerly incarcerated learners.

The Opportunity

MiCHEP seeks a Director of Strategic Initiatives and Operations to serve as the organization’s senior operational leader, including leading implementation of its four-year Ascendium-funded statewide initiative. This position combines strategic project leadership with a chief operating function: managing workplans and organizational systems, coordinating partners and consultants, overseeing contracts and payments, supporting personnel administration, and managing MiCHEP’s day-to-day relationship with its fiscal sponsor, Michigan College Access Network.

The Director reports to the MiCHEP President. Working with the MiCHEP Steering Committee and key partners, the President sets organizational strategy, leads funder and major external relationships, represents MiCHEP publicly, and retains final executive authority. The Director will translate that strategy into implementation and will have substantial authority to manage approved projects, budgets, systems, staff, consultants, and routine operational decisions.

The successful candidate will be a proactive and highly organized leader who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. This individual will anticipate needs, identify unresolved questions, coordinate people and resources, and take responsibility for ensuring that commitments become completed work.

Responsibilities

The Director of Strategic Initiatives and Operations will:

  • Lead implementation of MiCHEP’s Ascendium-funded initiative, maintaining an integrated workplan that identifies priorities, responsibilities, timelines, budgets, deliverables, and measures of progress.
  • Coordinate the work of member institutions, MDOC, MCAN, consultants, evaluators, government agencies, reentry and workforce organizations, and incarcerated and formerly incarcerated students.
  • Monitor progress, identify obstacles, recommend solutions, and ensure that organizational and grant commitments are completed on time.
  • Integrate the Ascendium initiative with MiCHEP’s other grants and priorities so that related projects reinforce rather than duplicate one another.
  • Prepare reports, briefings, agendas, decision documents, and project updates for the President, Ascendium, the MiCHEP Steering Committee, and other partners.
  • Support the President in funder and major partner conversations, attend meetings as appropriate, document decisions, and manage implementation and follow-through.
  • Serve as MiCHEP’s primary day-to-day administrative liaison with MCAN, which serves as MiCHEP’s fiscal sponsor and employer of record.
  • Manage the full administrative lifecycle of contracts, consultants, and vendors, including scopes of work, required documentation, approvals, signatures, deliverables, renewals, and records.
  • Prepare, submit, and track invoices, payment requests, reimbursements, consultant payments, and other financial transactions; reconcile internal records with MCAN reports and monitor grant budgets.
  • Coordinate with MCAN on position approvals, recruitment, hiring documentation, onboarding, payroll, benefits, leave, performance documentation, and other personnel matters.
  • Establish durable systems for project management, document organization, decision tracking, meeting preparation, internal communication, and organizational follow-through.
  • Plan and coordinate statewide convenings, mediated dialogues, working groups, site visits, and other collaborative activities.
  • Coordinate external evaluators and technical-assistance providers and connect project activities to performance measures and organizational learning.
  • Supervise additional MiCHEP staff as those positions are established and coordinate the work of consultants and project teams.
  • Ensure that incarcerated and formerly incarcerated students have meaningful opportunities to shape the initiative’s priorities and activities.

Qualifications

MiCHEP recognizes that strong candidates may arrive through different educational and professional pathways. An equivalent combination of education, professional experience, and lived expertise will be considered.

Competitive candidates will demonstrate:

  • At least five years of progressively responsible experience in organizational operations, project leadership, grant implementation, nonprofit administration, or a related area.
  • Experience managing complex initiatives involving multiple institutions or partner organizations.
  • Experience with contracts, budgets, payments, vendors, personnel processes, grants, or fiscal-sponsor relationships.
  • Strong judgment and a demonstrated ability to translate strategy into organized implementation.
  • Excellent writing, communication, and relationship-management skills.
  • The ability to anticipate needs, manage competing priorities, and advance work without continuous supervision.
  • Experience handling confidential financial, contractual, personnel, or organizational information with discretion.
  • The ability to navigate institutional complexity, disagreement, and competing interests constructively.
  • A demonstrated commitment to educational access, equity, human dignity, and the success of justice-impacted learners.
  • The ability to travel regularly within Michigan, including visits to correctional facilities.

Experience in higher education, corrections, workforce development, reentry, collective-impact initiatives, or systems-change work is preferred but not required. Familiarity with Michigan’s higher-education or criminal-justice landscape would be valuable. Lived experience with incarceration or the criminal legal system is welcomed and valued.

Compensation and Work Arrangements

The salary range is $80,000–$105,000, commensurate with experience, plus benefits administered through MCAN. MiCHEP anticipates hiring near the middle of the range but may consider compensation elsewhere within the range based on the successful candidate’s qualifications.

The position is primarily remote and requires regular travel throughout Michigan. It is funded through July 31, 2030. Continued employment beyond the grant period will depend on organizational needs and available funding.

Application

Please submit a résumé and cover letter through MCAN’s application system. Applications will be accepted for approximately 30 days. Review of applications will begin as they are received.

title: Automotive Flat Rate Technician
description:
Rogers Motors in Hermiston Oregon has full-time openings for Automotive Technicians across our Hermiston dealerships. Our employees are motivated, knowledgeable and caring professionals who build long-term client relationships. A hands-on style and a passion for doing what is right by our customers and our community is vital.

Rogers Motors has been a family-owned business supporting our local community for over 55 years. We provide training, mentoring, coaching, and full support to help you succeed. All full-time positions include medical and dental coverage, paid vacation, 401(k) & more. Rogers Motors is a drug-free, equal opportunity employer. Applicants must pass a background check and drug test while possessing a valid driver’s license with an acceptable safe driving record. If you want to join a winning team and continue to drive home the culture of success that we’ve built over the last 55 years, we want to speak with you!

OVERVIEW

The Automotive Technician performs routine repairs and maintenance ranging from warranty, recalls, scheduled maintenance and customer pay. It is imperative that these tasks can be performed at the highest quality to ensure customer retention as well as an outstanding reputation. A successful candidate for the Automotive Technician position will have at least 3 years of experience in an automotive repair environment.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Drivability, electrical diagnosis and air conditioning repairs.
  • Routine repairs and maintenance related to warranty, recalls, and scheduled maintenance.
  • Operate inspection software.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Valid Driver’s License and good driving record.
  • High school diploma or the equivalent.
  • At least 3 years of experience in an automotive repair environment including, heavy duty truck or automotive repair.
  • Must possess computer skills.
  • Must possess personal tools necessary to perform repairs.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • ASE Certifications or tech school degree preferred but not required.
  • Knowledge in all aspects of automotive repair and maintenance.
  • Ability to operate all shop equipment.
  • Self-motivated and capable of working efficiently with little supervision.
  • Excellent communication skills.

WORKING CONDITIONS

The Automotive Technician will stand six to eight hours per shift. Will lift parts weighing up to 50 pounds. Will be exposed to noise, vibration, dust, exhaust fumes, paint, and other hazardous and nonhazardous materials. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to complete each essential duty satisfactorily. The working conditions described above are representative of those an individual may encounter while performing the essential duties and responsibilities of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

title: Logistics Supervisor
description:
Working for Sara Lee:

Sara Lee Frozen Bakery became a stand-alone company in 2018 when it was purchased by Kohlberg and Company (private equity) from Tyson Foods. We have the feel of start up in many ways, though we are an established brand with a strong customer and consumer base. If you have an entrepreneurial spirit, continually seek process improvements and a strong sense of customer service, then this is the right type of environment for you.


Our vision is to be the world’s most beloved bakery by creating irresistible foods, growing with our customers, and delivering value for all. We believe that each of us has unique points of difference and experience to offer. We believe that there is always a better way, and we will never be satisfied with status quo. We believe simplicity enables speed. We believe in integrity above all. We live for food, and we “wow” consumers and customers through collaboration and innovation.

Summary:

The Logistics Supervisor’s job is to maintain direct control over all plant floor operations in the Shipping and Receiving area by supervising union hourly employees throughout their dealings with these functions. They also ensure that all steps are taken to positively influence supply chain from raw material receipt and issuance through to finished good reporting and shipments. The Logistics Supervisor must understand functions of NetSuite, MRP, DCS, and systems to help employees through them and work with other shifts and departments to meet preset goals. Finally, they are responsible for developing and maintaining several offline functions, such as recycling, load confirmations, pallet programs, and so on.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:


The position responsibilities outlined above are not to be construed as all encompassing. Other duties and responsibilities may be required and/or assigned as necessary.


Knowledge and Requirements:

All job offers are based on the conditions that the candidate can provide proof of authorization to work legally in the United States and pass a urinalysis screening, which is part of the post-offer health assessment. Candidate must be at least 18 years of age. Must be flexible with working hours and available for overtime when needed.

  • Direct work of hourly Union employees in S&R areas
  • Reconcile Inventories of both Raw Materials and Finished Goods
  • Work with crews on importance of Lot #’s in both areas for Trace, Hold, Recall
  • Conduct Safety and Quality communication meetings with crews; hold update discussions as needed, determine work schedules, overtime, open positions
  • Meet all S&R budget applications
  • Manage/Oversee shipping loads of FG, work with Traffic, Distribution, and Deployment on issues
  • Manage special projects such as, waste, pallets, supplies, inventories, computer systems
  • Oversee 2x a year raw material Inventories
  • Knowledge of food production processes a plus
  • Participate on plant cost savings team
  • Extensive knowledge of plant, policies, production needs, and labor relations
  • Cover entire range of plant floor dealing with all S&R employees on respective shifts
  • Ability to work any and all shifts, rotation is a strong possibility
  • Knowledge of Union contract, Safety, and Quality processes and procedures
  • Understanding of budgets and a drive to meet bottom line
  • Ability to reconcile and mange inventories
  • Effective Computer Skills
  • Able to manage large cross functional groups of Union employees in distinctly different areas


Education:

  • BS or BA in management, logistics, or related field a plus
  • Experience will be considered in lieu of a degree, especially in any situations involving supervision, warehousing, dock, etc.

Success Factors:

  • Computer proficiency including Microsoft Excel, Word, NetSuite, and Power Point. A good knowledge of accounting practices is helpful. Good systems person who can provide effective results working within DCS, MRP, DRP, and other modular systems (Netsuite and RF Smart experience is a plus).
  • A good knowledge of accounting practices is helpful.
  • Knowledge of Maintenance and parts and preventative maintenance programs.
  • Able to manage complex and time-sensitive projects to the satisfaction of different groups.
  • High initiative in problem solving.
  • Commitment to teamwork.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and projects simultaneously with numerous interruptions.
  • Must be self-motivated
  • Strong English verbal and written communications skills required.
  • Closely work and problem solve with other departments and various levels of Management and Union employees. Extensive knowledge of plant, equipment, policies, and labor relations.
  • Ability to use judgment when dealing with confidential issues. Able to provide top level service to both internal and external customers.
  • Ability to manage diverse cross functional groups to common goal.


Physical Demands:

  • Position is about split between floor time and office time
  • Quite a lot of computer work is required
  • Some time spent in coolers and freezers and outside yard


Work Environment:

  • The work environment characteristics are representative of those an employee encounters while performing essential job functions in a managerial/supervisory/technical/office capacity within a manufacturing environment.


Supervisory: Hourly union shipping and receiving staff report to this position


Travel: Approximate 0-5% travel required and ability to tour facilities and grounds.

Role Overview:


Responsible for providing triage, clinical support, and direct care to clients in acute and other bed-based care settings. This role delivers direct client care, crisis intervention, and assessment in collaboration with medical and clinical staff to maintain a safe and therapeutic environment for individuals experiencing behavioral health crises. The clinician works with a multidisciplinary team to support treatment goals, clinical and medical services, safety planning, and discharge coordination. Responsibilities also include conducting risk assessments (phone-based, on-site, and field-based), providing crisis interventions, coordinating care, offering brief interventions, resource navigation, and arranging external placements as needed. The position requires daily advocacy for diverse and often marginalized populations, ensuring interventions, support, and resources are delivered in an inclusive and equitable manner.


Primary Focus Areas

  • Crisis intervention
  • Behavioral health triage
  • Risk assessment
  • Mobile crisis response
  • Community resource navigation
  • Admission coordination
  • Care transitions and placement services


Essential Duties (Levels I–V):

  • Provide behavioral health crisis intervention, triage, and field/facility-based support to ensure safe and appropriate transitions of care.
  • Respond to crisis calls and community needs via phone, in person, and in the field, including dispatch and collaboration with Mobile Crisis teams.
  • Conduct rapid behavioral health and risk assessments, de-escalation, and brief therapeutic interventions to stabilize individuals in acute distress.
  • Determine appropriate level of care and coordinate dispositions, including hospital, residential, or community-based services, in collaboration with partners such as hospitals, law enforcement, and emergency services.
  • Develop and implement safety plans and short-term stabilization interventions with clients, families, and multidisciplinary teams.
  • Support intake, walk-in triage, and operations within Behavioral Health Urgent Care and other facility settings as needed.
  • Maintain timely, accurate clinical documentation in the Electronic Health Record (EHR).
  • Participate in multidisciplinary meetings, supervision, debriefings, and quality improvement activities.
  • Maintain a safe, trauma-informed, and therapeutic environment while responding to emergencies and supporting crisis operations.
  • Provide consultation and support to junior staff and contribute to coordinated team-based care across settings.


Minimum Qualifications:

Education, Experience, and Licensure

  • Experience working in a community-based behavioral health setting providing direct support and services to individuals with mental health and/or substance use challenges is required or preferred based on level. Advanced levels typically require two or more years of relevant experience.
  • Experience coordinating mental health interventions and services with community partners and external agencies is preferred.
  • Completion of the Colorado Behavioral Health Administration (BHA) Crisis Professional Curriculum through the OwnPath Learning Hub is required within 90 days of hire unless already Crisis Professional Certified.
  • Participation in a Substance Use Disorder training program is required upon hire where applicable.
  • Colorado Certified Addiction Specialist (CAS) certification is preferred or required for designated levels.
  • Current CPR and First Aid certification is required at hire or must be obtained within 30 days of hire.
  • Valid Colorado driver's license, or the ability to obtain one within 30 days of hire, is required. Employees must maintain an acceptable driving record and may be required to safely transport clients to appointments, community activities, treatment programs, and partner agency locations.

title: 2027 Conservation Assistant Crew Leader (Taos)
description:
ROCKY MOUNTAIN YOUTH CORPS

2027 Assistant Crew Leader Position Description

Upper Rio Grande Office (Taos)



Rocky Mountain Youth Corps (RMYC) is a nonprofit youth development organization serving New Mexico. We inspire young adults to make a positive difference in themselves and their communities. Through training and service, Corpsmembers discover their potential for healthy, productive lives.


POSITION PURPOSE:

Assistant Crew Leaders (ACLs) play a pivotal role in building successful crews and meaningful programming. They are leaders, facilitators, and communicators, tasked with inspiring fellow Corpsmembers to achieve personal and professional growth. As both a member of the crew and a part of the leadership team the ACL occupies a unique and demanding position. For the right individual, this position is a pathway towards full leadership positions and further opportunities in conservation.


POSITION TYPE: Seasonal, full time, exempt AmeriCorps member

SCHEDULE: Day work, Spike schedule, or Hybrid schedule.
Day work schedule is Tuesday-Friday, 7:00am-5:30pm with weekends off.
Spike schedule is Tuesday-Tuesday, 7:00am-5:30pm, camping at the project site. Spike is 8 days on shift followed by 6 days off. Hybrid schedule includes both spike work and day work.

STIPEND: $740 ($18.50/hr equivalent) per week before taxes, paid every two weeks.

EDUCATION AWARD: $5,176.50 upon completion of 1200-hour AmeriCorps Service Term

REPORTS TO: Crew Supervisor, with supervision by the Upper Rio Grande Conservation Program Coordinator

DATES: February 1, 2027 - November 12, 2027. 11 weeks of orientation training followed by project work

LOCATION: Taos, New Mexico with project locations throughout the state.

Rocky Mountain Youth Corps - 1321 Salazar Rd, Taos, New Mexico 87571

Participants must have reliable transportation to and from the RMYC office, according to their work

schedule for the duration of the season.


MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

Crew Leadership

  • In partnership with Crew Supervisor, assist in the creation of a highly collaborative leadership structure with shared responsibilities and input.

  • Help facilitate scheduled educational training throughout the season, while also assisting in impromptu “teachable moments” in the field.

  • Model appropriate professional behavior, environmental stewardship, and work ethic for Corpsmembers; be an example that inspires the crew.

  • Maintain a strong commitment to creating a culture of safety within the crew.

  • Assist with crew function during disaster relief work lasting up to 45 days (if deployed).


Project Management

  • Serve with Crew Supervisor, Program Coordinator, project sponsors, and organizational partners to accomplish projects in an efficient and timely manner.

  • Assist with leadership of the crew (or a portion of the crew) for project efficiency or as the need arises, under the direction and supervision of program staff. Examples include guidance with proper tool use, assisting with the organization of service tasks such as organizing a crew on a trail or thinning project, or helping to facilitate safety discussions with the crew. Assisting with leadership does not include direct supervisory tasks like discipline or timecard approval, which are handled solely by staff crew supervisors or other program staff.

  • Track daily tool issues, ensuring that tools are well-maintained, organized, and accounted for throughout project work.

  • Assist in daily preparation of supplies and equipment: first aid kits, vehicle inspection, personal protective equipment.


OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Assist in the facilitation of crew meetings on a regular basis.

  • Assist in reporting requirements and project impact paperwork.

  • Create a leadership development plan to further personal growth and leadership competencies.

  • Comply with all RMYC and AmeriCorps rules and policies and not participate in any prohibited activities as described in the member agreement.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED:

  • 18-30 years of age as of February 1, 2027

  • US Citizen, National, or Lawful Permanent Resident of the United States

  • Able to complete entire length of service term (see “dates” above)

Experience

  • Experience with, or an interest in, environmental or conservation related projects.

  • Community volunteer experience or a history of service-based learning.

Skills

  • Ability to perform strenuous physical tasks under adverse weather conditions

  • Good public speaking skills to address crews and conduct training sessions.

  • Strong organizational and communication skills, and the ability to be punctual and reliable.

Behavioral Competencies

  • Open to constructive feedback.

  • Flexibility and adaptability. Strong capacity as a team player.

  • Maturity level that allows for supervision and motivation of peers.

  • Ability to take initiative and follow through with project goals.


BENEFITS:

  • Healthcare coverage is available to all AmeriCorps members at no cost to the member. This is considered primary coverage and is not available as supplemental coverage.

  • A certain number of Non-Scheduled Days (paid days off) are available depending on the length of the term of service (These days off ARE NOT counted toward the service hours required for the Educational Award)

  • RMYC observes all National holidays and are considered paid days off, however RMYC reserves the right to have AmeriCorps members work or service hours on certain holidays if necessary to meet program requirements (These days off ARE NOT counted toward the service hours required for the Educational Award)

  • For AmeriCorps members serving a 1700 hour term of service, Childcare coverage is provided.

  • Student loan forbearance and interest payments are available for those who qualify

  • Access to the “Public Land Corps Hiring Authority” for members serving at least 640 hours.


PREFERRED EXPERIENCE / EDUCATION / CERTIFICATION:

  • Previous experience with Rocky Mountain Youth Corps or other youth development/conservation organization.

  • Leadership experience with peers, preferably in a mentoring or instructional capacity.

  • Knowledge of tool use and safety.

  • Proficient driving trucks, and/or 4x4 SUV with trailer attachment

  • Wilderness medicine certification (WFA, WFR).

  • Familiarity with techniques and concepts of safety and risk management.

  • Consistent positive mental attitude.


EVALUATION:

  • Members serving less than a full-time term of service (<1700 hours) will receive only an end-of-term evaluation


TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Periodic overnight travel and non-traditional work hours, inclusive of weekend and evening hours.


PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Lift or move up to 50 pounds occasionally, up to 20 pounds frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds constantly.

  • Frequently traverse uneven terrain; balance, stoop, kneel, reach, push, pull, and/or grasp.

  • Have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles and to determine the accuracy, neatness, and thoroughness of work assigned.

  • Receive detailed information through oral or signed communication; convey important instructions accurately and effectively.

  • Work outdoors, subject to outside environmental conditions.


Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.



Rocky Mountain Youth Corps is available to all and we will not discriminate or refuse services to any staff or member because of perceived or actual race, color, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, political affiliation, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital or parental status, military service or pregnancy.

RMYC is a drug free workplace. All RMYC positions depend upon funding availability.

title: Information Systems Security Engineer (ISSE)
description:
PID: 26-11-05-003


E-INFOSOL is seeking a highly motivated Information Systems Security Engineer (ISSE) to be a full-time employee in Huntsville, AL to join our innovative and customer solutions focuesed team.



Job Description:


The Information Systems Security Engineer (ISSE) supports the security, compliance, and authorization of information systems by implementing and assessing security controls, managing security documentation, and supporting the Risk Management Framework (RMF) process. This role works closely with System Owners, ISSOs, ISSMs, and Authorizing Officials to ensure systems meet security requirements, address vulnerabilities, and maintain accreditation. Responsibilities include reviewing security scans, developing security policies and procedures, implementing and maintaining security technologies, responding to cybersecurity incidents, and supporting cloud and enterprise environments.


The Information Systems Security Engineer will be responsible for the following:

  • Support the System Owner by working with or as the system ISSO to complete the security controls, provide artifacts, review the plans, create POAMs and help with using the GRC.
  • Test the controls, review the scans and create any authorization docs (ECs).
  • Develop and oversee the implementation of information security procedures and policies.
  • Build, maintain and upgrade security technology, such as firewalls, for the safe use of computer networks and the transmission and retrieval of information.
  • Design and implement appropriate security controls to identify vulnerabilities and protect digital files and electronic infrastructures.
  • Monitor and respond to computer security breaches, viruses, and intrusions.
  • May oversee the assessment of information security systems.
  • Respond to security requirements levied by the ISSM, AODR, and AO during the Security Assessment and Authorization process.



Required Experience:

  • Active Top Secret clearance
  • 7+ years of experience with modern networks, operating systems, databases, and virtual computing (Bash, Linux, or UNIX)
  • Expert technical knowledge in security engineering and IT systems engineering.
  • Experience with SAML
  • Development Software use (Oracle Java, Perl, and Python)
  • Experience with SQL
  • AWS Cloud Services


Education: (preferred)

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.



About E-INFOSOL

E-INFOSOL is a Service Disabled and Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) located in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area. We specialize in building modern and tailored solutions to support our customers’ mission. As a mission-first organization, we deliver Subject Matter Expertise (SME) in cloud computing, virtualization, cyber security, software development and data services. We support the Intelligence Community, Department of Defense, Federal Law Enforcement, Civilian Agencies and the Private Sector.


Through strategic partnerships with top industry players such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Broadcom, Microsoft and Cisco, E-INFOSOL provide an array of IT products and solutions. Combined with our industry expertise, we deliver in-depth knowledge on Government requirements and fully understand NIST and DoD security requirements. Our expertise in the latest technologies combined with our understanding of infrastructure needs and security requirements provides the best combination for achieving innovative and secure environments for Government Agencies and Private Sector.


Career Growth

“Putting People First, Achieving our Mission Together”. E-INFOSOL is a people-first organization focusing on a positive employee culture that inspires creativity and innovation in support of our customers. With opportunities such as reimbursement and bonuses based on completion of certifications, we invest in our employees’ career growth.


Job Type

  • On-site


Benefits

  • Medical – company subsidized premiums for employees, including family and dependent options
  • Dental and Vision
  • Retirement Savings (401k) up to 4% match
  • Health Savings Account (HSA), FSA and DCFSA
  • Company-paid Short/Long-term disability (w/ additional supplemental options)
  • Company-paid Life and AD&D (w/ additional supplemental options)
  • Generous Paid Time Off and ALL 11 Federal Holidays
  • Legal and Identity Protection Services
  • Bonuses for certifications and reimbursement

Employee Perks:

  • UberOne, Company Outings (Sporting events, Happy Hours, etc.), Discounts on services including Pet Insurance


Company Awards

  • SBA 8(a) Certified
  • SDVOSB

title: Content Development Associate I, Exams
description:
POSITION TITLE: Content Development Associate I, Examinations (multiple vacancies)


STATUS: Full time / Exempt


LOCATION: Chicago, IL (Hybrid: 2 days/week on-site, 3 days/week remote)



ABOUT NCSBN

The world leader in nursing regulatory knowledge, the National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN) is an independent, not-for-profit organization that empowers and supports nursing regulators. The organization protects the public and the trust in nursing through innovative regulatory solutions, insights and expertise. With its NCLEX® Examinations, Nursys® national licensure database and groundbreaking research, NCSBN attracts people who are passionate about what they do and driven by the knowledge that their work protects the public.


JOB SUMMARY

We are seeking a talented registered nurse (RN) to join our Examinations team. The ideal candidate will bring value to the team by contributing their nursing knowledge and expertise to assist in the content development process for all NCSBN examinations.


Reporting to the Manager, Content Development, Examinations, the Content Development Associate I will be able to work independently to review and edit nursing exam content, while also having the opportunity to interact with a team of content developers and nursing experts on various department projects. This position will play a large role in facilitating item writing and review panels, which include a variety of external stakeholders and nursing SMEs.


This role is an exciting opportunity for a skilled RN who has an interest in developing nursing licensure examinations in a professional setting. If you are looking to join an organization committed to advancing nursing regulation and policy worldwide, this could be a great fit for you!


RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Utilizes nursing knowledge to assist the content development process to ensure content is current, accurate, and legally defensible. Designs test questions, reviews and edits content, ensures validity and reliability, and aligns content with professional standards.
  • Facilitates and provides support for all aspects of item development sessions/panels as assigned. Leads group discussions, records and documents responses, and analyzes and summarizes results.
  • Assists in item content and item evolution, including testing security, item input, forms/document creation and maintenance.
  • Assist in the development of material for public speaking and outreach through internal and external presentations on behalf of NCSBN including speaking at workshops. Provides support to special assignments and innovative research projects related to test development.


QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor of Science in nursing degree required.
  • Unencumbered Registered Nurse (RN) license required.
  • Minimum of four years of experience in recent clinical practice required.
  • Experience with public speaking required.
  • Skilled in collaboration, time management, and multi-tasking skills.
  • Ability to travel as required.


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The anticipated starting salary for this position is $78,000 - $89,000 annually. Actual compensation will be dependent on a candidate’s relevant experience, skills, training, certifications/licenses, qualifications and geographical location.


NCSBN offers eligible employees a competitive benefits package that provides our team members with plan options to meet their individual needs. Review benefit details here:


TO BE CONSIDERED

Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their resume as soon as possible.


The National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN) is an equal employment opportunity employer. Decisions affecting employment are considered without regard to disability, race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, genetic information, military or veteran status, sexual orientation, marital status or any other protected characteristic.

title: Supply Chain Specialist

title: Range Safety Officer
description:
JOB PURPOSE

Assist customers at the range and ensure a safe environment.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Provide the very best in customer service
  • Be knowledgeable of products and firearms safety
  • Keep the range clean and safe at all times
  • Enforces range safety policies to ensure safety of patrons
  • Identifies patrons creating hazardous shooting conditions and tactfully corrects safety violators
  • All other duties, as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS

Required Qualifications:

  • A high school diploma or equivalent
  • Ability to multi-task and work under limited supervision
  • Ability to wok under stressful conditions
  • Prior Range Safety Officer experience

title: Staff Scientist I - TLM
description:
QPS’ Translational Medicine (TLM) Department seeks a Staff Scientist I!

Do you want to be part of an organization that is making a difference in the lives of millions of people worldwide? If so, we want to hear from you!


As a Staff Scientist I in TLM, you will be a key contributor in a laboratory role focused on the analysis of drug or other targets in complex biologic matrices using immunologic methods. Responsibilities will include laboratory stewardship, wet-lab operations as well as data reduction and documentation.


QPS’ Story:

Since its inception, QPS has been assisting pharmaceutical, biotechnology and medical device companies with their drug development efforts by providing a full range of Neuropharmacology, DMPK, Toxicology, Bioanalysis, Translational Medicine, Early Phase Clinical and Phase II – IV Clinical Research services. To meet the needs of our clients, we strive to employ talented, caring and committed individuals who will work collaboratively towards achieving our mission of improving human health and the quality of life.


Team members enjoy challenging and rewarding work and are encouraged achieve their best. Underpinning the operation is a culture that values diversity, innovation, accountability, teamwork and a friendly atmosphere where performance is recognized and rewarded. We provide unique company benefits, training, and advancement opportunities. Most importantly, we value each of our team members as employees and as individuals.


If this sounds like your ideal work environment, then we would love to speak with you, so apply today! Please visit our website () for more information and to see all current openings.


Please note - this role is not eligible for visa sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants should already have permanent or fully unrestricted authorization to work in the United States


The Job

  • Set-up, use and maintain complex, state of the art, instrumentation
  • Proficiently execute complete assays, daily and independently, in accordance with the GLPs and governing policies and SOPs to avoid failed runs and study findings
  • Document results, accurately record observations, and maintain study records in accordance with the GLPs and governing policies and SOPs to avoid failed runs and study findings
  • Prepare report documents and author final sample analysis (SA) reports
  • Prepare data tables and/or write reports


Work Location

  • This job will be 100% QPS-office/facility based


Requirements

  • Combination of relevant education & experience that provides sufficient knowledge & skills to ensure incumbent’s success in this role, such as:
    • University/college degree in a relevant scientific discipline (such as biology, chemistry, pharmacology or related) and/or
    • Relevant experience in a CRO, clinical research, or regulated laboratory environment preferred
  • Desire to learn and grow professionally, with demonstrated ability to work with increasing independence

  • Exposure to FDA or other regulated industry laboratory is preferred


Why You Should Apply

  • Great learning opportunities, especially for those new to the field. Our seasoned professionals are here to support and work with you to explore your learning potential and career goals.
  • Structured Career Ladders that provide excellent growth based on your personal aspirations.
  • Bonuses and merit increases are a part of the QPS total rewards approach and are linked to individual, team and company performance.
  • Solid Benefits package, including Company-matched 401(k), and Company-sponsored Group Life/AD&D and Short and Long-term Disability Insurance
  • Park-like setting in Newark, Delaware
  • Internal committees designed with the needs and enjoyment of QPS employees in mind.

In accordance with federal, state, and local laws, we recruit, hire, promote and evaluate all personnel without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, citizenship status, physical disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Job applicants and present employees are evaluated solely on ability, experience, and the requirements of the job. Building a world where LGBT people thrive as healthy, equal, and complete members of society.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • California P.O.S.T. training

Applications are encouraged from all persons regardless of their race, color, ancestry, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, sex, pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions, religion, disability, age, military or veteran status, including status as a victim of domestic violence, assault or stalking, genetic information (including family medical history), political affiliation or activities, medical or health conditions, and marital status.

title: Principal Software Engineer
description:

POSITION SUMMARY:

Supervises the nutritional aspects of patient care. Provides nutrition education/counseling to both inpatients and outpatients. Coordinates clinical nutrition with food service operations for delivery of patient care. Prepares and oversees implementation al all therapeutic diets and approves the diet manual. Attests to the nutritional adequacy of all foods served. Additional services may include community group presentations, education and participation in health fairs. Review of electronic medical record may be done off site. Onsite service is required for outpatient consultations, nutrition staff meetings and occasionally as requested by clinical staff.


POSITION REQUIREMENTS:

Minimum Education Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Dietetics or Nutrition from an accredited institution.

Other

  • Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics registration.

Licensure Required

  • State of Nevada Licensure.

Minimum Work Experience

  • Minimum 1-year healthcare experience preferred.

POSITION ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Collects and interprets nutritional data necessary to recommend, prescribe, or modify therapeutic diets as needed to meet the nutritional needs of patients:

  • Reviews patient's data for diagnosis, age, sex, height, weight, laboratory data, history, medications and other pertinent information.
  • Evaluates nutritional status of patients at nutritional risk and formulates individual care plans based on assessments.
  • Collaborates with other healthcare team members (medical staff, nursing, pharmacy, social workers, etc.) to plan and implement diet therapy as necessary in meeting the nutritional needs of patients. This is done either by phone or at times on site.
  • Evaluates data collected and completes nutritional consults/assessments as required following diet therapy standards.
  • Ability to be available as needed, including weekends and holidays.

Ensures proper nutritional management of patients with specialized dietary needs or who are at moderate to high nutritional risk:

  • Accurately calculates and develops meal patterns for specific therapeutic diets as appropriate.
  • Accurately modifies menus for patients with specialized dietary needs or complex diet prescriptions.
  • Monitors patient’s adherence to and tolerance of the nutrition care provided according to department standards and the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics.
  • Evaluates and monitors patient tolerances to enteral and parenteral therapies and recommends modifications as needed.
  • Selects and recommends appropriate type and method of nutritional support based on physiologic requirement and results from nutrition screen.
  • Determines appropriate oral or tube feeding formula to meet specific nutrient requirements.
  • Demonstrates the knowledge and skills necessary to provide care appropriate to the age of the patient served.

Teaches nutrition intervention principles to promote disease management and/or prevention:

  • Provides patient, family and caretaker dietary counseling and instruction, as requested by nursing or physician.
  • Educates nursing and medical staff about nutrition related topics as requested.
  • Plans and conducts group classes on nutrition related subjects for patients, public and professionals as requested.
  • Reviews and/or develops patient education materials.
  • Provides outpatient nutrition counseling services. Teaches nutrition intervention principles to promote disease management and/or prevention.
  • Completes required documentation and charge entry for outpatient services per facility procedure.

Documents all relevant aspects of nutritional care in the patient medical record:

  • Records nutritional assessment data and develops nutrition care plans for individual patients based on department standards.
  • Makes recommendations for nutrition intervention according to acceptable diet therapy guidelines.
  • Enters chronological notes that document changes and/or progress toward nutritional goals.
  • Accurately calculates and records nutrient intake analysis data on patients as needed.
  • Provides patient, family and caretaker dietary counseling and instruction, as requested by nursing or physician.

Coordinates clinical nutrition with food service operations for delivery of patient care:

  • Approves the therapeutic diet manual.
  • Approves all diets, patient menus and nutritional supplements.
  • Assists with the writing/revision of modified and house diets.
  • Evaluates menus for nutritional adequacy.
  • Provides in-service education regarding therapeutic diets to dietary staff. Provides guidance/training to dietary staff in the preparation and serving of therapeutic diets as necessary.
  • Attends department staff meetings, and other hospital meetings as required.
  • Aids in development and revision of department policies and procedures.
  • May be asked to assist in development and administration of clinical nutrition quality assurance program.
  • Participates in evaluation of dietetic services.

title: Advanced Full Stack Developer
description:

At Rincon Research Corporation, our primary business is innovating, developing, and fielding digital signal processing (DSP) products and services for the United States Defense and Intelligence Communities in support of national security.

Rincon Research Corporation seeks a Full Stack Developer to create cutting edge software and cloud computing solutions to challenging national security and defense signal processing, geolocation, and communication problems. You will work in a multi-disciplinary R&D environment with similarly skilled and motivated electrical engineers, mathematicians, and computer scientists/engineers in a highly rewarding personal and professional environment.

Come join the team that is creating cutting edge signal processing, geolocation, and communication systems for the future!

What are the primary responsibilities in the Advanced Full Stack Developer position?

Core responsibilities include leading the design and implementation of data systems with both web and database components, analyzing and maintaining existing databases and web interfaces, and adding new features to operational systems. This will include implementing signal processing and other algorithms with efficient software, testing with real data, providing applications to front-line customer facilities, and creating effective user interfaces and data visualization tools. A key responsibility is staying up-to-date with the latest technologies, tools, and methodologies and experimenting with new technologies to incorporate innovative solutions into RRC projects. RRC personnel can expect to work across all functional areas: systems engineering, development, integration and test, deployment and O&M, and experience the direct mission feedback from the customer and seeing your project provide real-world contributions that make a significant difference. You’re encouraged and expected to propose things that you believe will improve the applications and frameworks you’re working in. The ability to work unsupervised with minimal direction and the ability to self-start is a must.

What required background will make you successful?

  • Degree (Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD) in Computer Engineering or Computer Science
  • Minimum 8 years' experience in full-stack application development
  • Experience building scalable web applications using modern frontend and backend technologies
  • Experience designing and consuming RESTful APIs
  • Strong understanding of relational databases and data modeling
  • Proficient in modern software engineering practices for testability and readability

Preferred background:

Where is the position located?

This position is located at our Centennial, CO; Chantilly, VA; Colorado Springs, CO office or our Tucson, AZ Headquarters. Remote work/telework is not available for this position.

*The likely salary range for this position is $133,000 to $178,000,000. This is not, however, a guarantee of compensation or salary. Rather, salary will be set based on experience, geographic location and possibly contractual requirements and could fall outside of this range.

title: NUCLEAR MED TECH | NUCLEAR MEDICINE
description:
About the Role:

The Nuclear Med Tech plays a crucial role in the healthcare team by performing diagnostic imaging procedures using radioactive materials. This position is essential for providing accurate and timely results that assist physicians in diagnosing and treating various medical conditions. The Nuclear Med Tech will ensure patient safety and comfort while adhering to strict protocols and regulations regarding radiation exposure. Additionally, this role involves maintaining and calibrating imaging equipment to ensure optimal performance and accuracy. Ultimately, the Nuclear Med Tech contributes significantly to patient care and the overall effectiveness of the radiology department.



Minimum Qualifications:

  • Graduate Nuclear Medicine program
  • Current certification with Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification Board (NMTCB) or certification eligible post-graduation from a Nuclear Medicine Program. If registry eligible, must complete the certification with a passing grade within one month following hire date.
  • BLS and ACLS certification required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Nuclear Medicine Technology or a related field.
  • Experience in a clinical setting, particularly in a radiology department.
  • Additional certifications in advanced imaging techniques.

Responsibilities:

  • Assist physicians during exams along with obtaining nuclear images for interpretation.
  • Maintaining high quality of professionalism in dealing with patients.
  • Perform nuclear medicine procedures, including SPECT scans, ensuring adherence to safety protocols.
  • Prepare and administer radiopharmaceuticals to patients, monitoring their reactions and providing necessary care.
  • Maintain and troubleshoot imaging equipment, ensuring it is functioning correctly and safely.
  • Document and report imaging results accurately, collaborating with physicians to discuss findings.
  • Educate patients about procedures, addressing any concerns to ensure a positive experience.

Skills:

The required skills for this position include a strong understanding of nuclear medicine principles and the ability to operate complex imaging equipment. Attention to detail is crucial, as the Nuclear Med Tech must ensure accurate preparation and administration of radiopharmaceuticals. Excellent communication skills are necessary to effectively educate patients and collaborate with healthcare professionals. Problem-solving skills are also important for troubleshooting equipment issues and addressing patient concerns. Preferred skills, such as advanced imaging techniques, enhance the tech's ability to provide comprehensive care and improve patient outcomes.

title: Seasonal Club Transportation Specialist
description:
Position Title: Seasonal Club Transportation Specialist (September-June)

Location: The Fall Line, Butler, GA

Department: Lodging

Status: Seasonal Part Time

About The Fall Line

The Fall Line is a premier private destination golf and sporting club located in Southwest Georgia. Our club offers state-of-the-art facilities, including two Ogilvy, Cocking and Mead designed 18-hole golf courses, a 9-hole short course, and world-class facilities for shooting, hunting and angling. In addition to our outstanding outdoor offerings, we pride ourselves on exceptional hospitality, with multiple dining and lodging options, all enhanced by our 25-acre farm that is the centerpiece of 4,500-acre property.

Position Overview

The Seasonal Club Transportation Specialist plays a critical role in ensuring a seamless guest experience across all areas of The Fall Line. This position supports the Hospitality, Housekeeping, and Transportation teams by maintaining clean, well-stocked facilities and providing professional, safe transport for members and guests throughout the property.

Key Responsibilities

  • Safely operate company vehicles including SUVs and Sprinter Vans to transport members and guests between lodges, residences, sporting venues, and other locations across the property.
  • Provide baggage handling services, including the delivery, loading, and unloading of luggage, golf bags, and personal items.
  • Assist with golf club bag transport and storage, ensuring proper handling and guest readiness.
  • Maintain cleanliness and readiness of all vehicles, including interior and exterior cleaning, fueling, and basic maintenance checks.
  • Support the Housekeeping and Facilities teams with linen delivery, restocking of supplies, and general upkeep of common areas.
  • Respond promptly and professionally to guest requests, ensuring a high level of service and discretion.
  • Assist with setup and breakdown of special events, seasonal transitions, and other operational projects as directed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned in support of The Fall Line’s hospitality and operations standards.

Qualifications

  • Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (required).
  • Previous experience in hospitality, guest services, or transportation preferred.
  • Strong customer service skills with a professional, polished demeanor.
  • Ability to lift and move heavy luggage, equipment, and furnishings safely (up to 50 lbs).
  • Flexible schedule with availability on weekends, holidays, and evenings as required.
  • Must demonstrate reliability, attention to detail, and the ability to maintain confidentiality.

Work Environment

This role requires working outdoors in various weather conditions, operating vehicles across uneven terrain, and interacting frequently with guests and members. Professional appearance and demeanor are essential at all times.

Seasonal Work Schedule

This is a Seasonal Full-Time position with an anticipated employment season of September through June.

Work hours are based on Club usage and operational needs and may fluctuate throughout the season. Employees should anticipate reduced hours during periods of lower Club activity, particularly during December through February. Additional hours, including overtime when authorized, may be available during periods of peak Club usage.

The position requires flexibility to work early mornings, evenings, weekends, holidays, tournaments, and special events as scheduled.

Employment during a future season is anticipated based on business needs and satisfactory performance but is not guaranteed.

Drug-Free Workplace

The Fall Line is committed to maintaining a safe, healthy, and drug-free workplace. As a condition of employment, applicants who receive a conditional offer may be required to successfully complete a drug screening. Employees are also subject to drug and alcohol testing in accordance with company policy and applicable law.

The Fall Line participates in Georgia’s Drug-Free Workplace Premium Credit Program.

description:
JOB OVERVIEW
The Claims Analyst II is responsible for managing shortage, damage and transportation claims, coordinating insurance and other settlements including vendor recovery. This position will also assist in continuous improvement of efficiency for claims related activities, while supporting the alignment of processes and practices across all locations while assisting the manager with department projects and initiatives as required and assigned.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
This position does the following in accordance with all applicable Federal, State and local laws / regulations and the Company’s policies, procedures and guidelines:

Independently manages shortage, damage, and transportation claims from initiation through resolution, ensuring timely dealer credit issuance, claim settlements, and adherence to KTC guidelines and procedures.
Manages vendor charge-back claim reviews and recovery efforts, investigating claim validity and maximizing settlement outcomes with vendors and third-party providers.
Conducts complex cross-functional investigations involving Accounting, Finance, Legal, Warranty, and other business partners to validate reimbursement claims, assess liability exposure, ensure due diligence, and maintain accurate records in support of organizational and regulatory requirements.
Manages carrier claims across multiple transportation modes, (TL, LTL, Parcel, Ocean, Air)
coordinating directly with carriers to resolve disputes and protect company financial interests.

Supports inventory recall and rework projects, conducting investigations and coordinating corrective actions to minimize operational disruptions.
Work directly with KTC distribution centers or 3PLs to quickly close gaps in performance related to freight loading / securement practices. Collaborate on continuous process improvements.
Served as a departmental resource by providing guidance, training, and operational support, while maintaining readiness to assume higher-level responsibilities as needed.
Supports special projects, operational initiatives, and cross-functional efforts while maintaining ownership of claims management, reporting, and process improvement activities.

QUALIFICATIONS

High School Diploma/GED with a minimum of five (5) years of experience in the claims management industry required.

Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Supply Chain, or Transportation with a minimum of three (3) years of experience in the claims management industry preferred.

Claims management training, insurance recovery or settlement practices required.

Strong knowledge of Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SAP, or equivalent ERP system

Good writing and communication skills; strong work ethics; analytical skills

Strong Logistics & transportation knowledge

Claims Management knowledge, preferably within the Heavy Industry segment

Customer Service experience

Experience working with 3PL, carriers and service providers

Ability to interact with all company departments

Uses effective oral and written communication skills; delivers information in a clear and concise manner, listens and communicates effectively with others.

Requires sufficient personal mobility and physical reflexes, to permit the employee to function in a general office environment and accomplish tasks and duties as outlined above.

If you want to join a winning team and continue to drive home the culture of success that we’ve built over the last 50 years, we want to speak with you!

OVERVIEW

The Quality Inspection Technician - Entry performs basic maintenance and repairs to customer vehicles. A successful candidate for the Quality Inspection Technician - Entry position will be mechanically inclined, enjoy working on vehicles, and have a good work ethic. There are no tools or formal training required for this position. Opportunities for paid training and career advancement exist for this position!

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Inject grease into units, such as springs, universal joints, and steering knuckles, using hand or compressed-air powered grease gun.
  • Inspect fluid levels of steering gear, power steering reservoir, transmission, differential, rear axle housings, and shackles.
  • Check air pressure of tires.
  • Lubricate moving parts with specified lubricants.
  • Drain oil from crankcase and refill with required amount of oil.
  • Spray leaf springs with lubricant, using spray gun.
  • Add water to radiator and battery.
  • Replace oil and air filters.
  • Sell lubrication and safety inspection services and maintain related records on regular customers, following up periodically with telephone, mail, or personal reminders.
  • Perform duties that are work related as directed by manager or lead technician.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Valid Driver’s License.
  • High school diploma or the equivalent.
  • Two years of experience as a technician's helper or apprentice in an automotive dealership.
  • Manual dexterity.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Knowledge in all aspects of automotive repair and maintenance.
  • Good work ethic.
  • Positive, hard-working attitude, with good judgment.

WORKING CONDITIONS

This is a physically demanding position. The Quality Inspection Technician - Entry will stand six to eight hours per shift. Will lift parts weighing up to 70 pounds. Will use spray gun. Will stoop, kneel, crouch, crawl, reach, handle, and feel. Will be exposed to noise, vibration, dust, exhaust fumes, and other hazardous and non-hazardous materials. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to complete each essential duty satisfactorily. The working conditions described above are representative of those an individual may encounter while performing the essential duties and responsibilities of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

title: Facilities Administrator
description:
Why Join Rincon Research Corporation (RRC)?


At Rincon Research Corporation, our primary business is innovating, developing, and fielding digital signal processing (DSP) products and services for the United States Defense and Intelligence Communities in support of national security.

Rincon Research Corporation seeks a Building Maintenance Technician who will oversee operation, repair, and maintenance on all building systems in such a manner as to ensure optimal conditions at our Chantilly, Virginia facility, and who will provide facility administration support for day-to-day site operations, including remote facility administration support for our sites located in Colorado, Florida, and Arizona.

Come join the team that is creating cutting edge signal processing and geolocation systems for the future!

What are the primary responsibilities in the Facilities Management and Logistics Specialist position?


Facilities Engineering

  • Oversee the operation and scheduled maintenance of HVAC and electrical equipment, plumbing systems, and building interior repair.
  • Work with outside vendors on scheduled maintenance of various building systems.
  • Work with colleagues and tenant customers to complete work orders and resolve building system issues.
  • Respond to after-hour unscheduled emergencies, when needed.
  • Perform other basic tasks as required, such as hanging bulletin boards, changing bulbs, setting up office furniture, janitorial services, etc.
  • Comply with all applicable codes, regulations, governmental agency and company directives related to building operations and work safety.
  • Oversee and inspect work performed by service vendors and contractors to ensure compliance with contracts. Routine vendors include janitorial, landscaping, security, life safety, HVAC, plumbers, and electricians.
  • Routinely inspect building systems including fire alarms and extinguishers, HVAC, EMS system, and plumbing to ensure operation of equipment is within design capabilities.

Facility Administration

  • Maintain facility records and documentation, including equipment manuals, warranties, building drawings, and inspection reports, ensuring files are current.
  • Administer the facility work order system: log, prioritize, assign, and track service requests through completion.
  • Coordinate vendor contracts, service agreements, purchase orders, and invoice processing for facility-related services.
  • Schedule preventive maintenance, inspections, and vendor site visits, and maintain the facility maintenance calendar.
  • Track facility expenditures against budget, obtain vendor quotes, and assist with annual facility budget planning.
  • Maintain safety and compliance records (fire/life safety inspections) and support space planning, office moves, and furniture coordination.

Logistics Specialist

  • Managed end-to-end receiving, inspection, tagging, storage, and tracking of incoming equipment and materials using Costpoint and eQuip, ensuring accurate inventory and property records.
  • Coordinated domestic commercial and military shipments by packaging materials to regulatory standards, selecting cost-effective carriers, and preparing required shipping documentation, including DD Form 1149.
  • Maintained accountability for U.S. Government property in compliance with FAR Part 45, Clause 52.245-1, tracking property movements and supporting multi-agency government property audits.
  • Conducted annual physical inventories, reconciled discrepancies, processed returns and carrier claims, and maintained organized warehouse operations to ensure inventory accuracy and operational readiness.
  • Collaborated with contracts, finance, customers, and internal teams to resolve logistics issues, support equipment receipt and distribution, and provide logistics and property management assistance.


What required background will make you successful?

  • A minimum of 3+ years’ experience working with building operations, including a basic understanding of HVAC, electrical, plumbing, etc.
  • Knowledge of OSHA standards and local codes.
  • Valid driver’s license.
  • Ability to frequently walk up and down stairs for inspections.
  • Ability to detect emergency alarms auditory and/or visual.
  • Ability to access hard-to-reach areas, including getting on hands and knees as needed for equipment inspections.
  • Ability to safely climb ladders.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.
  • Ability to bend, squat, reach, and kneel on a daily basis.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain TS/SCI security clearance
  • US CITIZENSHIP REQUIRED

Where is the position located?

This position is located at our Chantilly, VA office.

*The likely salary range for this position is $40 - $50 per hour. This is not, however, a guarantee of compensation or salary. Rather, salary will be set based on experience, geographic location and possibly contractual requirements and could fall outside of this range.

What benefits does RRC offer?

  • 100% employer-paid premiums for family medical and dental insurance, employee life insurance, short-term and long-term disability (STD & LTD)
  • Flexible reimbursement spending accounts for medical expense and dependent care
  • Immediate participation and vesting in the company’s Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) and 401(k) Plan
  • Employer contributions to RRC’s ESOP
  • Employer matching contributions to the company’s 401( k) Plan
  • Employer discretionary contributions to the company’s 401(k) Plan


Rincon Research Corporation is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected factor.
